name: Ultramarine
poem: Beyond the sea, from a single mountain in Afghanistan — lapis lazuli ground finer than gold and reserved for the robe of the Virgin.

recipe.note: A pure, saturated blue carrying a trace of violet.

lenses.label: Art History
lenses.intro: Until synthesis was achieved in 1826, ultramarine cost more than gold by weight — and Renaissance contracts specified its use in the same breath as gold leaf.

entries.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
entries.blurb: Vermeer lavished costly ultramarine on the girl's turban — an extravagance that left him insolvent at death, his widow forced to pay his baker in paintings.

entries.title: The Wilton Diptych
entries.blurb: Eleven angels and the Virgin's mantle — all painted in a single uninterrupted field of ground lapis, the most lavish use of ultramarine in English medieval art.

entries.title: IKB 79
entries.blurb: Klein patented his own ultramarine — International Klein Blue — and spent the rest of his short life painting flat monochrome canvases with it.

lenses.label: Fashion
lenses.intro: A colour that has never quite stopped meaning luxury — every century reinvents its claim to ultramarine.

entries.title: The Virgin's Mantle
entries.blurb: By Church convention the Virgin Mary's robe had to be painted in ultramarine — the most precious pigment available, used to honour the highest subject.

entries.title: Schiaparelli Shocking
entries.blurb: Schiaparelli's signature shocking blue and pink reset luxury away from quiet good taste — a Surrealist's use of ultramarine as deliberate noise.

entries.title: Klein Blue Couture
entries.blurb: Klein had naked models pressed against canvas in his ultramarine — and convinced Pierre Cardin to translate the colour onto evening wear.

lenses.label: Nature
lenses.intro: True ultramarine comes from one mountain — and the journey of the stone is half the story.

entries.title: Sar-i Sang Mine
entries.blurb: The lapis lazuli mines have been worked continuously for seven thousand years — almost every drop of ultramarine in European art came from this single valley.

entries.title: Lapis Lazuli
entries.blurb: Deep blue lazurite veined with golden pyrite, formed when limestone is metamorphosed by sulfur-rich magma — a stone that already looks like a night sky.

entries.title: Blue Morpho
entries.blurb: The wings carry no pigment at all — microscopic scales scatter light to produce one of the most saturated blues on Earth. Underneath, the wings are brown.

lenses.label: Pop Culture
lenses.intro: Ultramarine never lost its association with the unreachable — even after synthesis made it cheap, it kept its mystique.

entries.title: YInMn Blue
entries.blurb: The first new inorganic blue discovered in two centuries — accidentally synthesised by chemistry students looking for something else entirely.

entries.title: Crayola "Ultra Blue"
entries.blurb: Crayola's 1990 colour renaming controversy — "Ultramarine" was simplified to "Ultra Blue" alongside complaints that crayons were losing their poetry.

entries.title: Blue Period
entries.blurb: A Japanese manga and anime about a teenager who falls in love with painting after seeing a single ultramarine work — colour as an awakening.

lenses.label: Etymology
lenses.intro: The colour's name is a directional — it tells you where the pigment came from before it tells you what it looks like.

entries.title: "Ultramarine"
entries.meta: Latin · ultra marinus — beyond the sea
entries.blurb: The literal meaning: the pigment came from beyond the sea — meaning Afghanistan, via Venice, by Mediterranean trade route. The name preserves the journey.

entries.title: "Lazaward"
entries.blurb: The Persian name for the lapis stone became Arabic "al-lazaward," then Old French "l'azur" — the same word produces both "lapis lazuli" and "azure."

entries.title: "French Ultramarine"
entries.blurb: The Société d'Encouragement offered 6,000 francs for an artificial ultramarine — Guimet won, but his pigment had to be marked "French" to distinguish it from the real thing.

lenses.label: Symbolism
lenses.intro: Ultramarine has always been a colour of the highest things — heaven, sovereignty, the unreachable.

entries.title: The Marian Blue
entries.blurb: Painting the Virgin in ultramarine was a theological choice as well as a financial one — the colour of the heavens, used to crown the Queen of Heaven.

entries.title: The Cosmic Blue
entries.blurb: Pre-photographic astronomers reached for ultramarine when they painted the night sky — the only pigment dark enough to suggest depth without falling into black.

entries.title: Le Bleu du Ciel
entries.blurb: Bataille's novel uses the colour of the sky as a synonym for vertigo — the unbearable, the beautiful, the colour of looking into nothing.
